purpose: Source boundaries for economy and preservation balancing; all exact simulation yields, shelf lives, budgets and mixed-food prices are authored tuning.

sources.supports: $700 post-wagon expenditure budget; F is amount spent on food, not pounds. Skilled hunt adds 52–58 food units, against 13/18/23 units per nominal fortnight; fort food credit is two-thirds of spending. No fresh-meat expiry ledger in inspected code.
sources.limits: Transcription with known issues. Not a historical commodity price list or 1985 executable.

sources.supports: Classic banker/carpenter/farmer starting budgets $2500/$1000/$400; hunting costs a day; resupply, changing rations and caution discussed.
sources.limits: Manual establishes behavior and game budgets, not actual emigrant occupational wealth or recovered source algorithms.

sources.supports: Designer explains 100 lb carry limit as a transport and wastefulness decision, and regional animals/cover/skill; later versions sometimes used 200 lb.
sources.limits: Do not infer a fresh-meat spoilage formula or compulsory preservation from the essay.

sources.supports: pp258–262: four yoke and 2500 lb guideline; five weighed staples total340 lb/adult, plus other goods including10 lb salt; St Joseph work cattle $25–30/yoke; emergency Hall/Boise flour $20/100 lb.
sources.limits: 1847 guide in1906 reprint, not1848 Independence mixed-food/salt receipt. Later mission resupply references are not1848 promises. Period advice contains bias and obsolete medicine.
